三味線或箏的領奏: Shamisen or koto taking the lead
三曲合奏的三件樂器各自有完整的獨奏傳統，合奏時不是「旋律加伴奏」，而是三條獨立的: The three instruments of sankyoku each have a complete solo tradition; in ensemble it is not melody plus accompaniment but three independent lines. The shamisen and the koto originally belonged to two separate circles, jiuta and sōkyoku, and sankyoku tied them together, with the shakuhachi joining from above.
三曲合奏的三件樂器各自有獨奏傳統，合奏時是三條獨立的線，靠錯位與留白交織，不是旋: The three instruments of sankyoku each have a solo tradition; in ensemble they are three independent lines, interwoven by displacement and by leaving space, not melody plus accompaniment.
三曲合奏的場合是宴席、茶事、舞台演出、地方節慶與學校的邦樂課程；地歌與箏曲的流派: Sankyoku is played at banquets, tea gatherings, stage performances, local festivals and school hogaku classes; the schools of jiuta and sōkyoku (Ikuta, Yamada and others) each have their own iemoto and training system, and concerts are mostly organised by the schools. The shakuhachi has schools such as Kinko and Tozan, a tradition of playing with koto and shamisen, and solo religious pieces (honkyoku).
三曲合奏的關鍵詞是「ずれ」（錯位）。三件樂器不是同時對齊同一個拍點，而是刻意讓旋: The keyword of sankyoku is ずれ, displacement. The three instruments do not line up on the same beat at the same time; instead the melodic lines are deliberately offset from one another: the shamisen's pluck slightly early, the koto's press slightly late, the shakuhachi's breath later still, so the three lines interweave rather than stack into a chord. This displacement in time, together with the microtones in pitch (the koto's oshi, the shamisen's oshi, the shakuhachi's meri and kari), is the core of hogaku ensemble and the hardest part to standardise. In the same piece, the size and timing of the pitch slides differ from school to school and player to player.
二十世紀的邦樂管弦樂團實驗，正是想把這個實踐變成一個組織。做法包括：把箏擴充成高: The twentieth-century experiments in a hogaku orchestra were exactly an attempt to turn this practice into an organisation. The methods included: expanding the koto into soprano, alto and seventeen-string bass koto; dividing the shamisen into treble and bass; adding a shakuhachi section, kokyū, percussion and Western instruments; and having a composer write a full score for a conductor to control. The new Japanese music movement pushed by koto players and composers in the early twentieth century brought koto and shakuhachi into Western chamber and orchestral line-ups. These experiments created a new repertoire and a new volume, but brought the same tension with them: microtones written out, displacement lined up, school differences flattened into one unified sound. Even today the hogaku orchestra is not mainstream, and most hogaku ensemble is still chamber scale, three to ten players, held together by school and by teacher-student lineage.
低音也一直是問題。十三弦箏的低音有限，十七絃箏與低音箏是為了補低音而設計的，但它: The bass has always been a problem too. The thirteen-string koto has a limited bass; the seventeen-string and bass kotos were designed to add low notes, but they are plucked and decay fast, so they cannot support a long note; the kokyū can sustain but is quiet. Large ensembles therefore often borrow Western cellos and double basses, or make up the difference with amplification. This is the same structural problem as the bass predicament of the Chinese orchestra, the Korean orchestra and the mandolin orchestra, except that hogaku's solution leans towards not solving it — keep the line-up small and let each instrument keep its own volume and timbre.
先聽錯位。三味線、箏、尺八是不是同時對齊同一個拍點；邦樂合奏的張力就在稍微錯開的: Listen for displacement first. Do the shamisen, koto and shakuhachi line up on the same beat at the same moment; the tension of a hogaku ensemble lies in the slight offset.
十三弦箏為基本；在合奏裡演奏與三味線錯開的旋律線，常以「替手」的方式另寫一條對位: The thirteen-string koto is the base; in ensemble it plays a line offset from the shamisen, often adding a second contrapuntal part by the kaede (substitute-hand) method
和韓國國樂管弦樂團相比，差別在是設計還是實踐。韓國團把傳統樂器家族化、補上低音、: Compared with the Korean gugak orchestra, the difference is design versus practice. The Korean orchestra turns traditional instruments into families, adds a bass, reads full scores and is controlled by a conductor, with new works and arrangements at its centre; hogaku ensemble keeps a chamber scale of three to ten players, does not standardise its instruments, and is held together by school and lineage. The twentieth-century hogaku orchestra experiments borrowed the organisation of the orchestra but never became mainstream, which is the exact opposite of the Korean case.
地歌與箏曲原本是兩個圈子。地歌是三味線的自彈自唱，曲子分為以歌為主的歌物與以器樂: Jiuta and sōkyoku were originally two circles. Jiuta is shamisen song with the player accompanying himself, its pieces divided into utamono, which are mainly song, and tegotomono, which are mainly instrumental interludes; sōkyoku is the koto's solo and song tradition. Sankyoku sets the two side by side: usually the shamisen plays the melody first, then the koto writes a separate contrapuntal line by the kaede method, and the two lines are not a doubling of one melody but independent, meeting only occasionally. Once the shakuhachi joins, the relationship is looser still: it can play the melody, or play only long notes and passing tones, filling the gaps between the plucked instruments. This relation of each independent, interwoven by displacement, is the biggest difference between sankyoku and a modern chamber group.
尺八與箏在合奏裡是伴奏關係。: The shakuhachi and the koto are in an accompaniment relationship in ensemble.
從上方加入，演奏與三味線同步或變體的旋律線，並以長音、滑音與氣聲補足撥弦無法持續: Joins from above, playing a line in sync with the shamisen or a variant of it, and making up with long notes, slides and breath sounds what the plucked strings cannot sustain; volume and timbre vary by school
日本邦樂合奏（Hogaku Ensemble）— 以箏、三味線、尺八為核心、在合: Hogaku Ensemble — a Japanese traditional ensemble built around koto, shamisen and shakuhachi, swinging between ensemble and solo. Ensembles and instrumentation by Next Door Sound Weavers.
曲目以地歌、箏曲、尺八本曲與三曲合奏曲為主；二十世紀以後增加了新日本音樂的作品、: The repertoire is mainly jiuta, sōkyoku, shakuhachi honkyoku and sankyoku pieces; after the twentieth century came works of the new Japanese music, concertos for koto and shakuhachi, and chamber music with Western instruments. The repertoire of the large hogaku orchestra is mostly new works, arrangements and film and television scores, performed in concert halls and at cultural events rather than at school recitals. At the amateur level, the keiko (teacher-student) system for koto and shamisen is still the main channel of transmission, and school clubs and community classes also offer an entry.
最常被拿來對照的是雅樂。兩者都是日本宮廷或流派傳承的音樂，差別在編制是否固定，以: The most common comparison is with gagaku. Both are music passed down by the Japanese court or by schools, and the difference is whether the line-up is fixed and who gives the time. Gagaku has a fixed three-wind line-up, instruments that are not made into families, and a repertoire that neither grows nor shrinks; the tempo is locked by the taiko and kakko, and the players perfect the ornaments within a fixed structure. Hogaku ensemble varies in number with school, piece and occasion: sankyoku can be three people, or it can add a seventeen-string koto and a shakuhachi section; the tempo is decided by the lead player's breathing and by the phrasing of the words, and no percussion locks the beat.
比較小編制與大編制。三到五人的三曲合奏與幾十人的邦樂管弦樂團，是兩種不同的音樂實: Compare a small line-up with a large one. A sankyoku group of three to five and a hogaku orchestra of several dozen are two different musical practices, not an enlarged version of the same thing.
沒有指揮；速度與段落靠領奏的呼吸與歌詞的句讀: No conductor; tempo and sections rest on the lead player's breathing and on the phrasing of the words
箏的調弦、三味線的調弦、尺八的指法都有嚴格的流派規範；微分音與滑音是刻意做出的音: The koto's tuning, the shamisen's tuning and the shakuhachi's fingerings all have strict school rules; microtones and slides are deliberately made musical content, not error. Writing them into equal temperament is what would change the music.
聽微分音。箏的按弦、三味線的押し、尺八的メリ與カリ，這些音高滑動是音樂的內容，不: Listen for microtones. The koto's pressing of the string, the shamisen's oshi, the shakuhachi's meri and kari — these pitch slides are the content of the music, not out of tune.
聽留白。三件樂器不是同時發聲，注意它們怎麼在彼此的空隙裡交替。: Listen to the space. The three instruments do not sound at once; notice how they alternate in each other's gaps.
聽調弦。同一首曲子換一種箏的調弦或三味線的調弦，整個音程關係都會改變。: Listen to the tuning. Change the koto tuning or the shamisen tuning for the same piece and the whole set of intervals changes.
胡弓是拉弦，音色柔和、帶鼻音，能持續發聲，與撥弦樂器的顆粒感形成對比；十七絃與低: The kokyū is bowed, with a soft, nasal timbre and the ability to sustain, contrasting with the grain of plucked instruments; the seventeen-string and bass kotos are products of the twentieth century, designed to extend the low range
自彈自唱；撥弦的顆粒與歌詞的抑揚互相咬合，是地歌的核心: Song with the player's own accompaniment; the grain of the pluck and the rise and fall of the words interlock, which is the core of jiuta
與中國國樂團相比，差別在音律的處理。國樂團用十二平均律與固定音高，把地方樂種的音: Compared with the Chinese orchestra, the difference is the treatment of tuning. The Chinese orchestra uses twelve-tone equal temperament and fixed pitch, flattening the intonation of regional genres; in hogaku ensemble the microtones, the tunings and the displacement are the content of the music, and writing them into equal temperament would change the piece.
這個表最重要的訊息是「沒有固定編制」。箏可以一台，也可以好幾台；尺八可以一支，也: The most important message of this table is that there is no fixed line-up. The koto can be one instrument or several; the shakuhachi one or a whole section; the shamisen can be sung and played by one person, or played without singing. The number is decided by school, piece and occasion, not by a line-up standard. This is the most fundamental difference between hogaku ensemble and the Chinese orchestra or the Korean gugak orchestra: the former is a collection of practices, the latter an organisation that was designed.
邦樂合奏就是日本的傳統樂團，編制固定。: Hogaku ensemble is the Japanese traditional orchestra, with a fixed line-up.
邦樂合奏沒有固定的編制數字。三曲合奏可以是三個人，也可以加十七絃、胡弓、尺八群；: Hogaku ensemble has no fixed number of players. Sankyoku can be three people, or it can add a seventeen-string koto, a kokyū and a shakuhachi section; the large hogaku orchestra is a twentieth-century experiment, not a continuation of tradition.
邦樂合奏（邦楽合奏，hogaku ensō）指的是以箏、三味線、尺八為核心的日本: Hogaku ensemble (邦楽合奏, hogaku ensō) means the Japanese traditional ensemble forms built around koto, shamisen and shakuhachi, above all sankyoku (koto, shamisen, shakuhachi). Its biggest difference from the line-ups above is that it has no standardised orchestra and no fixed number of players — the same word, ensemble, can mean three people or several dozen. From the twentieth century there were experiments that enlarged hogaku instruments and imitated the orchestra, but they never became mainstream.
邦樂的音高不準，是因為樂器沒有標準化。: Hogaku is out of tune because its instruments are not standardised.
音律不是平均律。箏的調弦依曲目而定，平調子、雲井調子等不同的調弦方式會改變整個樂: The tuning is not equal temperament. The koto's tuning depends on the piece: different tunings such as hirajōshi and kumoi jōshi change the instrument's whole set of intervals; the shamisen has honchōshi, niagari and sanagari, and the same instrument retuned is another world. The shakuhachi's pitch is controlled by breath and by covering the finger holes, so one fingering can produce different pitches. In ensemble these are not errors but the content of the music. To put such music into a large line-up, the first thing sacrificed is these microtones: with many players the timing of the slides cannot be unified, so they are written out or left out.
音量是第二個問題。三味線的撥弦、箏的撥弦、尺八的吹奏，三者的音量都有限，而且衰減: Volume is the second problem. The shamisen's pluck, the koto's pluck and the shakuhachi's blowing are all limited in volume, and they decay in different ways. Ensemble relies on leaving space — letting each instrument sound in the others' gaps rather than all pushing at once. This balance rests on the ear and on school training, not on a conductor. As the number of players grows, the space disappears, the players have to start counting beats and watching gestures, and the character of the music changes with them.
